smallholdings.name: Smallholdings
smallholdings.flavor: A hedge, a cow, and a name on the roll.
smallholdings.text: Worked farms and pastures gain +1 food and +1 gold.

expansionistGranaryLevies.name: Granary Levies
expansionistGranaryLevies.flavor: A new mouth arrives with two hands.
expansionistGranaryLevies.text: When a city grows in population, gain 15 production

theNaturalists.name: The Naturalists
theNaturalists.flavor: They counted everything and ate none of it.
theNaturalists.text: Each city gains +1 science for every two hills or mountains in its borders, at most +3.

thePatientHarvest.name: The Patient Harvest
thePatientHarvest.flavor: The granary waits better than the barracks does.
thePatientHarvest.text: Cities retain 30% of the food spent on growth, but produce military units 15% more slowly.

theFishTraps.name: The Fish Traps
theFishTraps.flavor: Stone walls in the shallows, and the tide does the rest.
theFishTraps.text: Once drafted, workers may tend a lake or coastal tile into fish traps for one charge: +1 food and +1 production. No chair required.

sweetWater.name: Sweet Water
sweetWater.flavor: Build where the water is good, and the rest follows.
sweetWater.text: Towns beside a river or lake gain +1 happiness. Worked freshwater tiles gain +1 food.

theSeedGrain.name: The Seed Grain
theSeedGrain.flavor: Every new village is given a sack of the best seed.
theSeedGrain.text: Towns you found start with one extra citizen.

theSpiritsOfPlace.name: The Ambarvalia
theSpiritsOfPlace.flavor: The procession walks three times around the fields before the sowing.
theSpiritsOfPlace.text: Your capital gains +1 faith. Each town gains +1 faith for every two improved tiles in its borders.

theRopeStretchers.name: The Rope Stretchers
theRopeStretchers.flavor: Two pegs and a knotted rope, and the field is laid out.
theRopeStretchers.text: Each town gains +1 science for every three improved tiles in its borders.

theBeatingOfTheBounds.name: The Beating of the Bounds
theBeatingOfTheBounds.flavor: Once a year the parish walks its edges, so nobody forgets where they are.
theBeatingOfTheBounds.text: Each town you found claims one extra wild hex of your choice next to its borders.
theBeatingOfTheBounds.note: For now the town takes the hex its borders would have grown into next, rather than one you choose.

thePyramidBuilders.name: The Pyramid Builders
thePyramidBuilders.flavor: When the river covers the fields, the farmers go to work on the king's stones.
thePyramidBuilders.text: +25% production toward wonders in your capital.

theRoadHome.name: The Road Home
theRoadHome.flavor: Every new town is one road away from the old ones.
theRoadHome.text: Each town you found is joined to your nearest town by road.

theWorkGangs.name: The Work Gangs
theWorkGangs.flavor: When the harvest is in, the village sends its young men to the roads.
theWorkGangs.text: Towns of at least three citizens may spend a citizen to raise a worker. This shares the town's levy wait.

theWoodlandBands.name: The Woodland Bands
theWoodlandBands.flavor: They know every path under the trees, and the trees hide them.
theWoodlandBands.text: Your units ignore the extra movement cost of forest and jungle, and gain +2 strength while they stand in forest or jungle.

theFoundingFurrow.name: The Founding Furrow
theFoundingFurrow.flavor: The plough marks the wall before the first stone is laid.
theFoundingFurrow.text: Founding a town grants culture equal to five times the number of towns you hold.

theHorrea.name: The Horrea
theHorrea.flavor: A province with full granaries does not riot.
theHorrea.text: Each Granary you hold gives +1 authority.

levyOfTheLand.name: Levy of the Land
levyOfTheLand.flavor: The field gives up a son and calls it a harvest.
levyOfTheLand.text: Cities may spend one citizen to gain production equal to the food it took to grow that citizen. A city may levy once every five turns.

expansionistTinkersGuild.name: Tinkers' Guild
expansionistTinkersGuild.flavor: Nothing is worn out while a tinker is awake.
expansionistTinkersGuild.text: Workers you produce or purchase gain +1 charge.

theOldSongs.name: The Old Songs
theOldSongs.flavor: Unploughed ground keeps the older tunes.
theOldSongs.note: Open water your people work counts as unbuilt ground here: the game tells works from wild, and not land from sea.

theLocalCensus.name: The Local Census
theLocalCensus.flavor: Count the working hands; the rest is opinion.
theLocalCensus.text: A town working at least four improved or tended tiles costs one less authority, minimum one.

theWildOrchards.name: The Wild Orchards
theWildOrchards.flavor: Nobody planted these trees, and everybody picks from them.
theWildOrchards.text: Once drafted, workers may tend a forest or jungle tile into a wild orchard for one charge: +1 food and +1 gold. No chair required.

theBurningSeason.name: The Burning Season
theBurningSeason.flavor: Fire in the dry season, and green shoots after the rain.
theBurningSeason.text: Once drafted, workers may burn a grassland or plains tile for one charge: +1 food. Bare ground becomes burned country; an improvement on the tile stays. No chair required.

darkEarth.name: Dark Earth
darkEarth.flavor: Every year of ash and bone makes the soil a little blacker.
darkEarth.text: Worked farms gain +2 food once they have stood for 20 turns, and another +2 food once they have stood for 50 turns.

theThreeSisters.name: The Three Sisters
theThreeSisters.flavor: Corn to climb, beans to bind, squash to shade the ground.
theThreeSisters.text: Worked farms beside a plantation or a pasture gain +2 food and +2 production, once per farm.

theCommons.name: The Commons
theCommons.flavor: Land that belongs to everyone keeps everyone fed.
theCommons.text: Each town gains +1 happiness for every two wild tiles it works, at most +3.

theHardCountry.name: The Hard Country
theHardCountry.flavor: Those who settle where nobody wants to live keep what they find.
theHardCountry.text: Worked desert and tundra tiles gain +1 food and +1 production.

expansionistTheMasterBuilders.name: The Master Builders
expansionistTheMasterBuilders.flavor: The best masons learn their trade in the quarry.
expansionistTheMasterBuilders.text: Towns working at least three mines, quarries or lumber mills give +1 renown a turn, favouring great engineers.

outposts.name: Outposts
outposts.flavor: A hut, a fire and a flag, a day ahead of the settlers.
outposts.text: Workers may plant an outpost on a wild tile within three hexes of your border, for one charge. It claims its hex and the ring around it for your nearest town, and costs no authority. A town founded on an outpost keeps that land.

theProspectors.name: The Prospectors
theProspectors.flavor: Follow the colour in the stream up to the hill it came from.
theProspectors.text: Prospecting costs workers and explorers no charge. Worked mines on a seam you surfaced gain +3 production.

sixGardens.name: Six Gardens
sixGardens.flavor: One garden is a hobby; six are a way of life.
sixGardens.text: Needs tended land. Commission. Have six tended tiles. Then, for the rest of the game, tended tiles gain +1 culture. The card leaves its chair.

theForestKeepers.name: The Forest Keepers
theForestKeepers.flavor: A wood cut with care is a wood cut for a hundred years.
theForestKeepers.text: Lumber mills that have stood for twenty turns gain +2 culture.

thePloughTeams.name: The Plough Teams
thePloughTeams.flavor: Eight oxen to the plough, and the village owns them together.
thePloughTeams.text: Each town gains +1 food for every two improved tiles in its borders.

thePolis.name: The Polis
thePolis.flavor: A city is the right size when one herald can be heard in all of it.
thePolis.text: While you hold at most four towns, every town gains +25% food.

thePublicFountains.name: The Public Fountains
thePublicFountains.flavor: Where the water runs in the square, the town gathers.
thePublicFountains.text: Towns beside a river or lake gain +1 happiness for every four citizens, at most +3.

theWildMarches.name: The Wild Marches
theWildMarches.flavor: Past the last field, the land belongs to the old songs.
theWildMarches.text: +1 culture for every four wild hexes you own.

theQuietProvinces.name: The Quiet Provinces
theQuietProvinces.flavor: A province you never hear from is a province well governed.
theQuietProvinces.text: Each town gains +1 production for every three points of spare authority, at most +3.

theRoadTowns.name: The Road Towns
theRoadTowns.flavor: The road brings the trade, and the trade brings the town.
theRoadTowns.text: Towns joined to your capital by road gain +2 production.

theBuildersLevy.name: The Builders' Levy
theBuildersLevy.flavor: Every town sends a cartload of stone to the king's great work.
theBuildersLevy.text: Towns may spend a citizen to send production equal to the food it took to grow it to a world wonder being built in another of your towns.

theLabourFeasts.name: The Labour Feasts
theLabourFeasts.flavor: The work ends with a song, and the song goes on all night.
theLabourFeasts.text: Needs a levy. After a town spends a citizen on a levy, it gains +1 culture for every wild tile it works, for ten turns. At most once every ten turns.

theGleaners.name: The Gleaners
theGleaners.flavor: What the reapers leave, the poor may gather.
theGleaners.text: Needs a levy. After a town spends a citizen on a levy, it gains +3 food for ten turns. At most once every ten turns.

theGrainCensus.name: The Grain Census
theGrainCensus.flavor: Count the granaries, and you have counted the kingdom.
theGrainCensus.text: While seated, this card gains +1 production and +1 gold each time one of your towns grows past its largest size. It starts at +2 of each.

theGardenFrontier.name: The Garden Frontier
theGardenFrontier.flavor: The gardener goes first, and the border follows the garden.
theGardenFrontier.text: Needs tended land. Workers may tend unowned wild hexes up to two hexes beyond your borders. A hex tended there joins your nearest town.

theBurhs.name: The Burhs
theBurhs.flavor: A wall for every town, and a town for every wall.
theBurhs.text: Towns gain +3 defence for every defensive building in them, and +100% production toward defensive buildings.

commissionBreakTheSod.name: Commission: Break the Sod
commissionBreakTheSod.flavor: The first furrow is the hardest, and the rest follow it.
commissionBreakTheSod.text: Commission. Work twelve improved tiles at the same time. Then, for the rest of the game, your improvements count as having stood ten turns longer. The card leaves its chair.

theLandHunger.name: The Land Hunger
theLandHunger.flavor: Their towns fill the valley. Ours will fill the next one.
theLandHunger.text: While another empire holds more towns than you, your towns build settlers 25% faster, and your settlers gain +1 movement.

theMarlPits.name: The Marl Pits
theMarlPits.flavor: Dig the chalk from the hill, and spread it on the field below.
theMarlPits.text: When your workers finish a mine or quarry, each farm or pasture beside it gains +1 food for the rest of the game, at most +2 on one tile.

theAediles.name: The Aediles
theAediles.flavor: The aediles kept the streets, the baths and the grain, and every new roof was theirs to keep.
theAediles.text: While seated, this card gains +1 production and +1 culture each time you finish a public work. It starts at +2 of each.

theWatercourses.name: The Watercourses
theWatercourses.flavor: The river is only lent; the ditch is owned.
theWatercourses.text: Farms directly beside a river irrigate adjacent farms. Irrigated worked farms gain +2 production. Water does not relay beyond that first step.

theHighlands.name: The Highlands
theHighlands.flavor: Every seam in the hill is a lesson.
theHighlands.text: Mines and quarries on hills gain +2 science and +1 production.

theCoast.name: The Coast
theCoast.flavor: The sea is a field nobody has to plough.
theCoast.text: Worked fishing boats gain +3 food and +3 culture.

provincialCouncils.name: Provincial Councils
provincialCouncils.flavor: The province speaks, and is not always wrong.
provincialCouncils.text: Connected towns other than the capital cost one less authority, minimum one, and gain +1 happiness.

expansionistTheGrainDole.name: The Grain Dole
expansionistTheGrainDole.flavor: A fed city forgets what it was angry about.
expansionistTheGrainDole.text: Cities of at least ten population gain +4 happiness and retain an additional 20% of food spent on growth.

expansionistTheWaterworks.name: The Waterworks
expansionistTheWaterworks.flavor: A fountain in the square, and nobody leaves.
expansionistTheWaterworks.text: Aqueducts cost 33% less production. Towns with an Aqueduct gain +1 happiness for every four citizens, at most +3.
expansionistTheWaterworks.note: The saving on the aqueduct is paid as extra production toward it, which comes to the same price.

expansionistTheBreadbasket.name: The Breadbasket
expansionistTheBreadbasket.flavor: When the town is full, the grain goes to the frontier.
expansionistTheBreadbasket.text: A town told to stop growing adds its food surplus to its production.

migration.name: Migration
migration.flavor: People go where there is room.
migration.text: Every ten turns, each of your towns that is at its happiness limit sends one citizen to your smallest connected town that has room to grow.
migration.note: A town has no happiness of its own, so the game reads your empire's: every ten turns, while your empire has no happiness to spare, your largest town sends one citizen to your smallest town joined to your capital, if that town is smaller.

veteranColonies.name: Veteran Colonies
veteranColonies.flavor: Twenty years of marching, then a plot of land.
veteranColonies.text: A military unit standing in one of your towns may retire there: the unit is removed and the town gains one citizen.

theLandscapeGarden.name: The Landscape Garden
theLandscapeGarden.flavor: A garden made to look as if nobody made it.
theLandscapeGarden.text: Needs tended land. Tended tiles beside a great-person work or a wonder gain +3 culture.

theEngineersYards.name: The Engineers' Yards
theEngineersYards.flavor: The yard is where the plans meet the timber.
theEngineersYards.text: Manufactories gain +3 production. Worked farms, mines, quarries and lumber mills beside a manufactory gain +2 production.

theTendedCountry.name: The Tended Country
theTendedCountry.flavor: The field and the wood have always helped each other.
theTendedCountry.text: Needs tended land. Tended tiles gain +2 production.

theOldFields.name: The Old Fields
theOldFields.flavor: A field your grandfather dug still feeds your grandsons.
theOldFields.text: +1% food and production for every three works that have stood thirty turns, at most +30%.

theHedgerows.name: The Hedgerows
theHedgerows.flavor: The hedge keeps the cattle in and the birds busy.
theHedgerows.text: Needs tended land. Worked farms beside a tended tile gain +2 food, once per farm.

theGreatHouseholds.name: The Great Households
theGreatHouseholds.flavor: A household of twenty can raise a barn in a day.
theGreatHouseholds.text: Each town gains +2% production for every citizen it has, at most +30%.

theHarbourCities.name: The Harbour Cities
theHarbourCities.flavor: Every ship that docks brings a story with its cargo.
theHarbourCities.text: Coastal towns gain +1 culture for every two citizens.

theMilestones.name: The Milestones
theMilestones.flavor: Count the stones, and you know how far the empire reaches.
theMilestones.text: +1% gold and culture for every three road hexes you have paved, at most +30%.

theTeemingRealm.name: The Teeming Realm
theTeemingRealm.flavor: So many people that the roads are never empty.
theTeemingRealm.text: +1% science and culture for every ten citizens in your empire, at most +30%.

theLabourRolls.name: The Labour Rolls
theLabourRolls.flavor: The clerk writes down every name, and every name is a year of work.
theLabourRolls.text: Needs a levy. +1% production and food for every two citizens you have levied this game, at most +30%.

theTerracesOfMoray.name: The Terraces of Moray
theTerracesOfMoray.flavor: Each ring of the terrace keeps a different season, and the farmers learn them all.
theTerracesOfMoray.text: Towns beside a mountain may spend a citizen to gain science equal to the food it took to grow that citizen.

theColonists.name: The Colonists
theColonists.flavor: The crowded town sends its younger sons to found a new one.
theColonists.text: Towns of at least six citizens may spend a citizen to raise a settler.

theBookOfSettlements.name: The Book of Settlements
theBookOfSettlements.flavor: Every name in the book is a town that somebody walked out to found.
theBookOfSettlements.text: +3% production and gold for every town you have founded this game, at most +30%.

theManyHands.name: The Many Hands
theManyHands.flavor: Every town sends a cart of stone to the capital.
theManyHands.text: Your towns build empire buildings 3% faster for each town you hold, at most +36%.

theBurghers.name: The Burghers
theBurghers.flavor: Town air makes a man free, and a free man takes up a trade.
theBurghers.text: Towns of at least twelve citizens fill their guild bar half again as fast.

watchAndWard.name: Watch and Ward
watchAndWard.flavor: Every town keeps a watch by night and a ward by day.
watchAndWard.text: Needs a levy. Units a levy raised gain +5 strength in your own territory.

theWoodwrights.name: The Woodwrights
theWoodwrights.flavor: Timber is patience, taken all at once.
theWoodwrights.text: Forest and jungle chops grant 150% more production.

theCommonDomain.name: The Common Domain
theCommonDomain.flavor: The commons runs to where the walking stops.
theCommonDomain.text: Towns of at least ten population may work owned tiles one hex beyond their normal work radius.

seasonalLevies.name: Seasonal Levies
seasonalLevies.flavor: Take them in the winter and give the spring back.
seasonalLevies.text: Needs a levy. After a city spends a citizen on a levy, it gains +60% food for ten turns. A city can gain this at most once every twenty turns.

theLongTending.name: The Long Tending
theLongTending.flavor: A grandmother's garden feeds her grandchildren best.
theLongTending.text: Needs tended land. Tended tiles gain +2 food for every 25 turns since they were tended, at most +6.

theMountainSchools.name: The Mountain Schools
theMountainSchools.flavor: Thin air and long views make for clear thinking.
theMountainSchools.text: Towns with at least two mountains in their borders gain +15% science. Worked mines and quarries beside a mountain gain +2 science.

thePolders.name: The Polders
thePolders.flavor: God made the sea; we made the land.
thePolders.text: Workers may raise a polder on a coast tile that touches at least three of your land tiles, for two charges. A polder yields as a farm on grassland.

publicWorks.name: Public Works
publicWorks.flavor: Build it once, and build it for everyone.
publicWorks.text: A great engineer may spend its act in one of your towns to complete an Aqueduct there, or to raise terraces on every worked hill in its borders.
deferred: a great engineer may finish an aqueduct in a town, or raise terraces on its worked hills
publicWorks.note: A great engineer has no such act yet, and terraces belong to one leader alone.

aCourtOfEngineers.name: A Court of Engineers
aCourtOfEngineers.flavor: The king listens to the people who build his bridges.
aCourtOfEngineers.text: Gain +50% renown, but great-person offers contain only great engineers.

theWideCountry.name: The Wide Country
theWideCountry.flavor: Room to grow, and the will to fill it.
theWideCountry.text: Commission. Claim twelve hexes by outposts, cleared camps or buying while this card is seated. Then, for the rest of the game, your borders grow 25% faster. The card leaves its chair.

oldWorkings.name: Old Workings
oldWorkings.flavor: The old shafts run deep, and the miners know every turn of them.
oldWorkings.text: Worked mines, quarries and lumber mills that have stood for twenty turns gain +3 production.

theManors.name: The Manors
theManors.flavor: The hall, the mill, the church, and the fields around them.
theManors.text: Each town gains +1 production for every two improved tiles in its borders.

theRoyalForests.name: The Royal Forests
theRoyalForests.flavor: The king's deer, the king's oaks, and the king's poets to praise them.
theRoyalForests.text: Towns working at least three lumber mills gain +25% culture.

theMegalopolis.name: The Megalopolis
theMegalopolis.flavor: A city so large that a person can live a whole life and never see its end.
theMegalopolis.text: Towns of ten or more citizens gain +1 science and +1 production for each citizen.

plenty.name: Plenty
plenty.flavor: Every new mouth is fed, and still there is bread left over.
plenty.text: When a town grows, it gains production equal to five times its new population.

theMillWheels.name: The Mill Wheels
theMillWheels.flavor: The river turns the wheel, and the wheel does the work of twenty.
theMillWheels.text: Towns with a Watermill gain +15% production.

theQuitrents.name: The Quitrents
theQuitrents.flavor: A penny a year for each field, and the lord asks for nothing more.
theQuitrents.text: +1 gold for every two hexes you own.

theHallowedWoods.name: The Hallowed Woods
theHallowedWoods.flavor: Some groves are never cut, and everyone knows which ones.
theHallowedWoods.text: Towns working at least five wild tiles gain +25% culture.

theAssayOffice.name: The Assay Office
theAssayOffice.flavor: Weigh the ore, test the metal, and write the number down.
theAssayOffice.text: Each seam you surface grants 60 science.

theStationes.name: The Stationes
theStationes.flavor: A post on every road, and a soldier at every post.
theStationes.text: Land units gain +3 strength while they stand in a town connected to your capital by road.

theManagedWild.name: The Managed Wild
theManagedWild.flavor: The wild was never empty. It was always somebody's garden.
theManagedWild.text: Needs tended land. Each town gains +5% food for every tended tile in its borders, at most +25%.

theMita.name: The Mit'a
theMita.flavor: A year of service on the great works, and then home to the village.
theMita.text: Needs a levy. A citizen spent on a levy returns to its town twenty turns later.

theSlackSeason.name: The Slack Season
theSlackSeason.flavor: After the harvest there are hands to spare.
theSlackSeason.text: Needs a levy. Every twentieth turn, after the harvest, your towns may levy whatever their wait.

theTrainedBands.name: The Trained Bands
theTrainedBands.flavor: Drilled on the common every Sunday, and ready when the bell rings.
theTrainedBands.text: Needs a levy. Units raised by a levy start as Veterans.

theFreedomOfTheCity.name: The Freedom of the City
theFreedomOfTheCity.flavor: A city that size makes its own laws, and pays for its own walls.
theFreedomOfTheCity.text: The first time each of your towns reaches fifteen citizens, and again at twenty, it gains production equal to forty times its population.

theToppingOut.name: The Topping Out
theToppingOut.flavor: When the last stone is set, every town in the realm comes to the feast.
theToppingOut.text: Finishing an empire building grants each of your towns production equal to five times its population.

theTaxRolls.name: The Tax Rolls
theTaxRolls.flavor: Every household is counted, and every household pays.
theTaxRolls.text: When the world takes a census, gain gold equal to five times your citizens.

theOpeningOfTheRoads.name: The Opening of the Roads
theOpeningOfTheRoads.flavor: The first cart from the capital brings the market with it.
theOpeningOfTheRoads.text: When one of your towns is first joined to your capital by road, it gains production equal to twenty times its population.

theGreatColonies.name: The Great Colonies
theGreatColonies.flavor: The mother city sends out a third of her people, and they take her name with them.
theGreatColonies.text: Towns you found start with a third of the citizens of your largest town.

theRaisingOfTheLand.name: The Raising of the Land
theRaisingOfTheLand.flavor: Drain it, dig it, raise it, and it feeds you forever.
theRaisingOfTheLand.text: When a great engineer rushes the works in one of your towns, every improved or tended tile in its borders gains +1 food and +1 production for the rest of the game.

theAgeOfImprovement.name: The Age of Improvement
theAgeOfImprovement.flavor: Every field drained, every road straightened, every mill rebuilt.
theAgeOfImprovement.text: The bonuses your Orders give to improved tiles are doubled.

theWaterCourts.name: The Water Courts
theWaterCourts.flavor: The court decides who gets the water, and the water goes everywhere.
theWaterCourts.text: A farm joined to fresh water by a chain of your farms counts as having fresh water.

theComingOfTheWater.name: The Coming of the Water
theComingOfTheWater.flavor: The aqueduct reaches the town, and the fields drink first.
theComingOfTheWater.text: When a town finishes an Aqueduct, every farm in its borders gains +1 food for the rest of the game.

theMountainTerraces.name: The Mountain Terraces
theMountainTerraces.flavor: Where the goats walked, the barley grows.
theMountainTerraces.text: Your towns may work the mountains in their borders. A worked mountain yields 2 science and 1 production.

theStakedClaims.name: The Staked Claims
theStakedClaims.flavor: A stake at every corner, and a name on every stake.
theStakedClaims.text: Each town you found claims every unowned hex within two hexes of it.

theSovereignWrit.name: The Sovereign Writ
theSovereignWrit.flavor: The more the law reaches, the further it can reach.
theSovereignWrit.text: Spare authority's bonus to production and border growth has no ceiling: +10% for every five points.

theImperialRoads.name: The Imperial Roads
theImperialRoads.flavor: Where the road goes, the governor need not.
theImperialRoads.text: Towns joined to your capital by road cost no authority.

theCapitolia.name: The Capitolia
theCapitolia.flavor: Every town raises its own small copy of the Capitol.
theCapitolia.text: Each empire building you hold gives each of your towns +1 culture.

theCuraAquarum.name: The Cura Aquarum
theCuraAquarum.flavor: The water board in the capital sends the water down every road it built.
theCuraAquarum.text: Towns joined to your capital by road count as having an Aqueduct.

theLandsGreatWork.name: The Land's Great Work
theLandsGreatWork.flavor: The harvest raises the monument, and the monument eats the harvest.
theLandsGreatWork.text: The city building the Magnum Opus gains +5% production toward it for each of your towns of at least eight citizens, at most +40%.

theGardenOfTheWorld.name: The Garden of the World
theGardenOfTheWorld.flavor: The whole country one garden, and every hand a gardener.
theGardenOfTheWorld.text: Needs tended land. Tended tiles gain +2 food, +1 production and +1 culture. Towns working at least six tended tiles gain +3 happiness.

theHeartland.name: The Heartland
theHeartland.flavor: Every empire has one valley it would never give up.
theHeartland.text: Goal: one of your towns works twelve improved or tended tiles that each yield 5 or more in total. Reward: for the rest of the game that town costs no authority and gains +3 happiness and +20% food. The card then leaves its chair.

theCorvee.name: The Corvée
theCorvee.flavor: Every town sends hands to the one great building.
theCorvee.text: While one of your cities builds the Magnum Opus, each of your other towns of at least ten citizens may spend one citizen for it, once every five turns. The Opus city gains production equal to the food that citizen took to grow. This shares the town's levy limit.

theMasterOfWorks.name: The Master of Works
theMasterOfWorks.flavor: One man to sign the plans, and a thousand to raise them.
theMasterOfWorks.text: When a great engineer rushes the works in the city building the Magnum Opus, each of your towns with a manufactory also sends that city one turn of its own production.

thePhilosophersPeaks.name: The Philosophers' Peaks
thePhilosophersPeaks.flavor: From the summit, the whole argument is laid out below.
thePhilosophersPeaks.text: Each town gains +2 science for every mountain in its borders, at most +6.

theInheritanceOfFields.name: The Inheritance of Fields
theInheritanceOfFields.flavor: The field remembers every hand that worked it.
theInheritanceOfFields.text: Worked improvements and tended works that have stood for at least 60 turns gain +1 production. Tended ones also gain +1 culture.

theMeasureOfTheLand.name: The Measure of the Land
theMeasureOfTheLand.flavor: Count the land, and you know what the realm is worth.
theMeasureOfTheLand.text: Every town gains +1 science for every 25 hexes your empire owns, at most +10.

theMotherCity.name: The Mother City
theMotherCity.text: Your capital gains +5% production and +5% culture for each town you have founded this game.

theGeneralLevy.name: The General Levy
theGeneralLevy.flavor: When the war comes, every farm sends someone.
theGeneralLevy.text: Your towns may spend one citizen to raise their best melee unit. At peace a town may do this once every five turns, sharing the levy limit; while you are at war, once every turn. Units raised this way cost no upkeep inside your borders.

theGreatMigration.name: The Great Migration
theGreatMigration.flavor: Nobody stays hungry next to a full granary for long.
theGreatMigration.text: Every ten turns, each foreign town within three hexes of your border loses one citizen to your nearest town, if your town is happier and has room to grow.

theEncroachingFields.name: The Encroaching Fields
theEncroachingFields.flavor: A furrow a year, and in a lifetime the boundary has moved.
theEncroachingFields.text: Once every ten turns, each of your towns of at least twelve citizens takes one hex from the borders of a foreign town next to it, if nobody works that hex and your town is larger than the town that owns it.

theDomesdaySurvey.name: The Domesday Survey
theDomesdaySurvey.flavor: Every field, every ox, every plough, written down.
theDomesdaySurvey.text: Commission. Own at least 120 hexes and work at least 40 improved or tended tiles at the same time. Then, for the rest of the game, each town gains +1 science for each improved or tended tile it works. The card leaves its chair.

theTwoHarvests.name: The Two Harvests
theTwoHarvests.flavor: The field below and the orchard above.
theTwoHarvests.text: Needs tended land. Your worked farms, mines and lumber mills also count as tended for your cards, but not as wild.

theTheodosianWalls.name: The Theodosian Walls
theTheodosianWalls.flavor: The more people inside, the more hands on the walls.
theTheodosianWalls.text: Your towns gain +1 defence for every two citizens.

theGreatAqueducts.name: The Great Aqueducts
theGreatAqueducts.flavor: Every town with running water sends its best masons to the great work.
theGreatAqueducts.text: The town raising the Magnum Opus gains +5% production toward it for each of your towns with an Aqueduct, at most +40%.

theImperialHighways.name: The Imperial Highways
theImperialHighways.flavor: Every road in the empire leads to the great work.
theImperialHighways.text: The town raising the Magnum Opus gains +3% production toward it for every town joined to your capital by road, at most +45%.

theKeeps.name: The Keeps
theKeeps.flavor: A tower, a well and a wall, and the valley around them answers to all three.
theKeeps.text: Workers may build a Keep, one in each town. A Keep gains the yields of every tile around it, and units on its tile gain +5 strength.

thePublicGood.name: The Public Good
thePublicGood.flavor: What the town builds for everyone, everyone learns from.
thePublicGood.text: +1% science and culture for each public work you hold, at most +25%.

theGrovesAndTheStones.name: The Groves and the Stones
theGrovesAndTheStones.flavor: The old trees stood here before the altar did, and knew it.
theGrovesAndTheStones.text: Unimproved forests gain +1 faith, in a city with a Shrine.

claimByTheSpade.name: Claim by the Spade
claimByTheSpade.flavor: The border is wherever the ditch ends.
claimByTheSpade.text: Improving unclaimed land beside your border claims it for the nearest eligible city. Each hex first claimed this way grants that city 15 food and 10 gold. [Improvement-led claim.]
claimByTheSpade.note: A worker cannot yet build outside your borders, and nothing takes ground in for the town that reaches it.
deferred: works raised on open ground beside your border take that ground for the nearest town
the first claim of each place pays that town in grain and coin

theGrowingAnnals.name: The Growing Annals
theGrowingAnnals.flavor: Every birth is entered, and the ink is never dry.
theGrowingAnnals.text: While active, gains +1 science and +1 culture per turn whenever one of your cities grows in population, no cap.
deferred: the card keeps count of every citizen born and pays a little more each turn for it
theGrowingAnnals.note: Not built, and the one thing missing is small. A town remembers how many people live in it and not how many ever did, and the design pays only for growth past a town's own greatest — so a counter of plain growth would write the annals twice for one citizen a levy took and the fields gave back. A town's high-water mark is one number on the town and one comparison where it grows; the counter of growths waits on it and on nothing else.

thePioneersPortion.name: The Pioneers' Portion
thePioneersPortion.flavor: Send them out fed, or do not send them.
thePioneersPortion.text: +25% production toward settlers. A city founded beside a resource costs one less authority.
thePioneersPortion.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. Nothing yet prices a town by what its ground carries.
deferred: a town founded beside a resource asks less of your writ than any other
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theFieldAltars.name: The Field Altars
theFieldAltars.flavor: Where the good things grow, something is thanked.
theFieldAltars.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theForestGardens.name: The Forest Gardens
theForestGardens.flavor: The forest was a garden long before anyone noticed.
theForestGardens.text: Once drafted, workers may tend a forest or jungle into a forest garden for one charge: +1 food. The forest stays standing and can still be chopped, which removes the garden. No chair required.

plantedForests.name: Planted Forests
plantedForests.flavor: We put the wood back, row by row.
plantedForests.text: Workers may plant forest on eligible open land for one charge. It matures after fifteen turns. [Planting and maturity.]
plantedForests.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. Nothing may plant a wood, and a wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made — so there is no turn to write on it and nothing to measure a young one against. The planter is what makes a wood young; until one exists, neither half of this can be said.
deferred: a worker plants a wood on open ground of your own
a planted wood is young for a long while, and cannot be felled for timber until it is grown

thePrizeRolls.name: The Prize Rolls
thePrizeRolls.flavor: The herald lists what nobody else has.
thePrizeRolls.text: +1 renown for every unique luxury resource.
thePrizeRolls.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

oldGrowth.name: Old Growth
oldGrowth.flavor: These trunks were old when the road was new.
oldGrowth.text: Worked mature forests gain +1 food and +1 production. Chopping mature forest grants 50% more production.
oldGrowth.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. A hex now remembers when its works were raised, but a wood is not a work: one nobody planted has stood since the world was made, so nothing can tell a grown wood from a young one until something plants one.
deferred: a grown wood your people work feeds and builds better than a young one
felling a grown wood yields more timber than felling a young one

charcoalBurners.name: Charcoal Burners
charcoalBurners.flavor: Smoke goes up, and somebody calls it prayer.
charcoalBurners.text: Chopping forest or jungle also grants faith and culture each equal to 20% of its chop production.

theWoodlandEdge.name: The Woodland Edge
theWoodlandEdge.flavor: The best field is the one the wood still watches.
theWoodlandEdge.text: Worked ordinary improvements beside unimproved forest gain +1 production per adjacent forest, at most +2. Worked unimproved forests beside a farm gain +2 food, once per forest.
theWoodlandEdge.note: Held whole. A hex can be paid a helping for every wood in its ring now, but the works this card pays are the ordinary ones — and an improvement that is not a great person's work is a thing no ground condition can name.
deferred: works pay more for every wild wood standing next to them
a wild wood beside a field feeds better for it

theHighPastures.name: The High Pastures
theHighPastures.flavor: Above the last wall, the grass is ours.
theHighPastures.text: Your cities may work owned mountains within their work radius. Those mountains provide 3 production and 2 faith. [Workability exception, not movement permission.]
theHighPastures.note: No law can yet put a citizen on a mountain: what a town may work is a fact about the ground alone.
deferred: your people may work the mountains inside your borders
a worked mountain gives stone and devotion

theLandShapesUs.name: The Land Shapes Us
theLandShapesUs.flavor: Ask where a town was founded and you have asked everything.
theLandShapesUs.text: Cities gain their founding trait: river +3 food/+3 gold; coast +1 route capacity; hill +3 production/+3 defence; forest +3 science; desert +4 faith; tundra/snow +4 culture; plain +2 food/+2 production. Exactly one trait applies.
theLandShapesUs.note: Nothing writes down what kind of place a town was founded on, so nothing can give it one reward and refuse it the rest.
deferred: every town remembers the one kind of place it was founded on
each kind of place pays its town its own reward, and only ever one of them

theWorksShadow.name: The Work's Shadow
theWorksShadow.flavor: Great work throws a long shade, and things grow in it.
theWorksShadow.text: +1 culture on tiles adjacent to a great work.
theWorksShadow.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: ground beside a great one's work sings for it
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theOpenFurlongs.name: The Open Furlongs
theOpenFurlongs.text: Farms gain +1 production for every two adjacent farm tiles.
theOpenFurlongs.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished, and marked uncertain there. A hex is paid a helping for every field beside it now, but not for every second one of them.
deferred: a field builds better for every second field beside it
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theProvincialSchools.name: The Provincial Schools
theProvincialSchools.flavor: The seam is opened, and then explained.
theProvincialSchools.text: +1 science and +1 culture on improved resource tiles in cities with a national building.
theProvincialSchools.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready — the realm's single great houses can be named now — and the card is not.
deferred: worked seams teach and sing in a town that has raised an empire building
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

daughterTowns.name: Daughter Towns
daughterTowns.flavor: The mother town sends bread until the daughter can bake her own.
daughterTowns.text: While a town you found has fewer than five citizens, the town that trained its settler gains +3 food.
daughterTowns.note: For now the small town itself gains the food, because the game does not remember which town trained a settler.

theCuratorsRoll.name: The Curators' Roll
theCuratorsRoll.flavor: Somebody must know what the city keeps.
theCuratorsRoll.text: +1 renown for each great work worked by a city.
theCuratorsRoll.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The kinds of great one's work a town puts to use can be counted now, but a standing trickle counts the realm's towns and not the ground inside one.
deferred: your standing grows with every great one's work your towns put to use
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theCommonTreasury.name: The Common Treasury
theCommonTreasury.flavor: What one town spends, the road repays to all.
theCommonTreasury.text: A production levy also grants each other connected owned city production equal to 20% of the levy's original payout. Shared production cannot trigger another sharing payout.
theCommonTreasury.note: A city cannot yet spend a citizen on anything, so there is no levy for this to follow.
deferred: a levy of labour pays every other town joined to your capital a share of what it raised
what is shared out cannot be shared again

irrigationWorks.name: Irrigation Works
irrigationWorks.flavor: Water goes where it is told, once.
irrigationWorks.text: Workers may build irrigation works for one charge on eligible owned open land. Adjacent farms count as irrigated and gain +1 food when worked. irrigation works base yield: +1 food +1 science [New improvement; ordinary tile/resource restrictions apply.]
irrigationWorks.note: There is no such works to build, and no field can yet pass water to the next one.
deferred: a worker raises a waterworks on open ground of your own
fields beside it count as watered and feed better
the waterworks itself feeds and teaches

reclamation.name: Reclamation
reclamation.flavor: Cut it down and the ground forgets it was jungle.
reclamation.text: Clearing jungle changes its land to plains and grants 30 food in addition to normal chop production. [Underlying-terrain change; does not change hills or resources.]
reclamation.note: The ground under a wood never changes in this game. The worksheet is reworking this card besides.
deferred: clearing a jungle leaves open plain behind it
clearing a jungle fills the granary as well as the woodpile

theCoppice.name: The Coppice
theCoppice.flavor: Take the crown, leave the stool.
theCoppice.text: Chopping mature forest you planted leaves young forest standing. It matures again after fifteen turns and cannot be harvested while young.
theCoppice.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. A wood cannot be planted, and nothing regrows where one is felled — this card is the second half of a cycle whose first half does not exist.
deferred: felling a wood you planted leaves a young wood standing where it was
the young wood grows back in time, and gives no timber until it has

theHermitages.name: The Hermitages
theHermitages.flavor: He wanted nothing, and the ground gave it anyway.
theHermitages.text: Great-person works qualify for your unimproved-land card bonuses. Each great-person work also grants adjacent worked tiles +2 of each of its positive native yield types. [Native yields exclude card additions; no propagation.]
theHermitages.note: No card can change what another card's ground condition admits.
deferred: a great one's work counts as wild ground for your other laws
ground beside a great one's work shares in whatever that work provides

expansionistTheOldWays.name: The Old Ways
expansionistTheOldWays.flavor: Leave it alone and it pays you.
expansionistTheOldWays.text: Worked unimproved land gains +2 food and +2 gold. Worked ordinary improvements lose 1 production, to a minimum of zero. Great-person works are exempt from this penalty.
expansionistTheOldWays.note: A law may take from a hex, but nothing yet stops the taking at nothing, so ground with no labour in it would fall below nothing.
deferred: works lose a little labour, and never fall below nothing for it

theSteppe.name: The Steppe
theSteppe.text: pastures gain +2 production. Horse-dependent military units cost 25% less production.
theSteppe.note: The horse-dependent soldiers are the mounted ones the roster draws, ridden and shooting alike.

theFloodplains.name: The Floodplains
theFloodplains.flavor: The flood is a creditor who pays first.
theFloodplains.text: floodplain farms gain additional food equal to their native food yield before card additions and multipliers.
theFloodplains.note: A share of what a hex's own ground provides reaches every voice it speaks in at once, and this card means the grain alone. The worksheet is reworking the figure besides.
deferred: a field on the floodplain is paid again in grain for the grain its ground already gives

theStandingPatronage.name: The Standing Patronage
theStandingPatronage.flavor: The master's works are the crown's furniture.
theStandingPatronage.text: While slotted, this card gains +1 authority for every great person improvement created. Starts at +1 authority.
theStandingPatronage.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. A card may keep a running count of battles, of wonders and of coin spent, but not yet of the great ones' works.
deferred: the card keeps count of every great one's work raised while it sits, and widens your writ for each
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theWoodsmensMarch.name: The Woodsmen's March
theWoodsmensMarch.flavor: The trees are on our side, or near enough.
theWoodsmensMarch.text: Units gain additional +4 combat strength while fighting in either forest or hills (does not stack on forested hills). Units ignore terrain penalties from moving onto forest or hills.
theWoodsmensMarch.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. A strength line may be paid for hills and not for woods, and nothing excuses a column the cost of rough ground.
deferred: your soldiers fight harder in the woods and on the hills, and never for both at once
your soldiers walk into woods and hills for what open ground would cost
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theQuarterOfMasters.name: The Quarter of Masters
theQuarterOfMasters.flavor: Put two masters on one street and watch.
theQuarterOfMasters.text: Great works with an adjacent great work gain double yields. This never stacks.
theQuarterOfMasters.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: a great one's work standing beside another pays twice over, however many stand there
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theComplementaryProvinces.name: The Complementary Provinces
theComplementaryProvinces.flavor: Nobody is rich in one thing.
theComplementaryProvinces.text: Connected cities gain +5% production and +5% culture per different founding trait represented among your connected cities, at most +30% each. The Land Shapes Us need not be owned.
theComplementaryProvinces.note: Nothing writes down what kind of place a town was founded on, so nothing can tell how many different kinds your realm holds.
deferred: your joined towns build and sing better for every different kind of place your realm was founded on

theVariedCountry.name: The Varied Country
theVariedCountry.flavor: A table with one dish on it is not a table.
theVariedCountry.text: Cities working at least four distinct terrain or feature types gain +20% food, production, gold and culture.
theVariedCountry.note: Nothing counts how many different kinds of country a town works.
deferred: a town whose people work many different kinds of country prospers in every voice at once

theHarvestTithe.name: The Harvest Tithe
theHarvestTithe.flavor: The tenth sheaf, and the wild hedge that grew it.
theHarvestTithe.text: Worked farms beside unimproved land gain +3 gold, once per farm. Farms beside a mature unimproved forest also gain +2 production.
theHarvestTithe.note: Half built, and so held whole. A field beside wild ground can be paid for it, but a wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made — so the second half waits on planting, which is what makes a wood young enough to tell a grown one from.
deferred: a field beside wild ground is worth coin for it
a field beside a grown wild wood builds better besides

forestSanctuaries.name: Forest Sanctuaries
forestSanctuaries.text: Worked mature unimproved forests gain +2 culture and +2 faith. Cities working at least three demand 20% less population happiness.
forestSanctuaries.note: Held whole, on two counts. A wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made, so nothing can tell a grown one from a young one until planting exists — and nothing admits a town for the number of wild woods its people work.
deferred: a grown wild wood your people work sings and prays for you
a town working several of them asks less of your peace
